title: Embed + Rerank CLI trace & hypotheses
content:
Goal: keep a short CLI-style trace + reproducible commands I ran while chasing a pair of related issues: (1) sporadic dimension mismatch errors from the rerank endpoint, (2) simultaneous latency spikes (~2-4x) for small batches.

Symptoms observed (high level):
- Rerank endpoint sometimes returns 400 / 422 with message: "expected vector length 1024, got 1536". Happens ~1-3% of requests, not correlated to input size.
- Latency spikes in 2026-02-28 14:00-16:30 UTC window: p95 went from 120ms -> 420ms for small 4-item rerank requests.
- Correlation: many failing requests during same window had come from internal QA service that uses a short-lived CLI wrapper.

Raw CLI / curl reproducer fragments I used (sanitized tokens):
1) embedding generation (python + requests):

python -c "import requests, json; r=requests.post('https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'embed-alpha-1024','input':['foo','bar']}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACT'}); print(r.status_code); print(r.text)"

Observed: usually 200 with "embedding": [list len 1024]. On failure trace earlier, payload had len 1536 (see notes below).

2) direct rerank call (curl):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rerank-small-1024","query":"q","documents":[{"id":"a","embedding":[...length maybe 1536...?]}]}'

Error: HTTP 422, body: {"error":"vector length mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536","code":"invalid_input"}

3) trace with shapes/logging to capture server-received shape (using our internal curl proxy that injects X-Debug headers):
curl -v -H 'X-Debug: shapes' -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/rerank ... 2>&1 | tee rerank-shape-log.txt

Server side echoed: X-Received-Embedding-Shape: [1,1536]

Hypothesis log (fast jotting):
- H1: Client-side double-concat bug (QA CLI) — the CLI accidentally concatenates an extra vector (e.g. caching + live) before sending, inflating dim from 1024->1536.
  - Counter: same shape mismatch sometimes from other clients (not just QA CLI).
- H2: Serialization anomaly in our python embedding client: when using numpy array.tobytes() vs list(...) maybe some clients are sending raw binary mistakenly into JSON and server interprets as larger vector?
  - Counter: error text explicitly reports vector length, implying server parsed array fine.
- H3: Model variant switch / runtime mixing: our embedding model has two output widths (1024 and 1536) depending on quantization/profile. Smart routing/fallback might substitute a 1536-dim model for embeddings when primary is overloaded, but rerank service expects 1024.
  - Evidence: at 14:00-16:30 we observed autoscaler thrash and a routing policy change (see EMB-4123 notes)
- H4: Middleware (API gateway or proto marshaler) sometimes attaches token-level metadata array and our parser merges arrays instead of treating as metadata — accidental flattening.
  - This would explain cross-client occurrence.
- H5: Batching/KV cache edge-case: combined request batching code concatenated KV caches across items when cache present -> inflated vector sent downstream.

Timing/latency theory:
- Latency spikes coincide with short bursts of high retry traffic from the QA CLI (fast-retries) + our autoscaler flip. Batching algorithm switches to a slower path when batcher flush thresholds change under contention -> sudden p95 increase.
- Also noticed increased time spent in "serialize_embeddings" stage in traces (span name) during spike windows. Hypothesis: large unexpected vectors increase serialization time and memory pressure -> GC/paging -> latency bump.

Commands I ran to collect traces & metrics: (local envs, sanitized)
- curl tracing headers:
  curl -H 'X-Debug: traces,shapes' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.dev/v1/rerank -o out.json -w 'HTTP:%{http_code} T: %{time_total}\n'
- k logs on rerank-service pods with grep for request id from out.json: kubectl -n prod logs svc/rerank -c server | grep <request-id> -A 30
- grabbed evicted/pod restart events around 2026-02-28 via: kubectl get events --namespace prod --since=3h | grep -i eviction
- profile: perf/top/heap when repro locally: python -m cProfile rerank_client_test.py > profile.out

Notable server logs snippets I captured (sanitized):
- [2026-02-28T14:07:12Z] WARN rerank: received embedding len=1536 for model=rerank-small-1024 request_id=xyz
- [2026-02-28T14:07:12Z] ERROR api-gw: failed to route: model signature mismatch: expected 1024 but got 1536
- [2026-02-28T14:23:35Z] INFO batcher: flush path=slow path triggered, flush_reason=queue_size_threshold, avg_batch_size=12

Quick reproducibility plan (ordered):
1) Run a golden client that we control (py script calling embeddings->rerank) and log shapes right before send. Ensure it never mutates arrays. Run 10k requests at low concurrency to see baseline.
2) Re-run under QA CLI (same token) to see if shape differences appear. Add deterministic seed to embedding generator to compare vectors.
3) Force routing to fallback model (simulate node pressure) and check if embeddings dims change. We can do this by temporarily tagging certain nodes as drained in staging to trigger fallback policy.
4) Add extra instrumentation in rerank middleware to log 'incoming-embedding-dims' and the 'upstream-model-id' per request for 24h (sampling 1:10)
5) Run heap/alloc profiler on rerank-service during a controlled spike to validate serialization+GC hypothesis.

Short-term mitigations proposed (quick):
- Reject/validate incoming embedding shape early with a clear error and a telemetry event that includes upstream model id and client-agent header. (low risk, deploy via canary)
- Apply temporarily stricter routing to avoid fallback to 1536-dim models for rerank routes until we have a fix. (ops change)

What I still need / open questions:
- Do we have any cases where the embedding service intentionally outputs 1536 for the configured model id? Check model catalog + runtime mapping for embed-alpha-1024.
- Can we correlate client User-Agent/CLI version for failing requests? I captured some in SLACK:#embeddings thread but need more.
- Is there any prior metric where average embedding size changed historically? (search metrics store)

Notes to self (next steps):
- @Jorge: can you add 2 fields to rerank request logs: upstream-model-id and client-agent?
- @Li: can you grep model-catalog and runtime-mapping for anything that would output 1536 under fallback?
- Schedule 1-hour pairing with infra to run the staged draining test Monday morning (low traffic).

Appendix - minimal repro payloads (use these to test):
- embeddings payload (python): {
  "model": "embed-alpha-1024",
  "input": ["quick test"]
}
- rerank payload (curl): {
  "model": "rerank-small-1024",
  "query": "quick test",
  "documents": [ { "id": "d1", "embedding": [0.0, 0.0, ... 1024 floats ...] } ]
}

This doc is a scratchpad — will migrate notes to EMB-4123 when we have a repro or a specific fix plan.
summary: Scratchpad tracing dimension-mismatch + latency spikes for embeddings->rerank. Contains CLI commands, raw errors, hypotheses, and a short repro/mitigation plan.
